note: The change in observed frequency when a wave source and observer move relative to one another. Approaching light shifts toward blue; receding light shifts toward red.

short: The sky imagined as a great overarching vault.
note: A literary word for the heavens or apparent arch of the sky.

short: Conventionally, Earth’s orbital reference plane.
note: Conventionally, the plane containing Earth’s orbit around the Sun, used as a reference for celestial positions and orbital inclinations.

short: Orbiting once per rotation of Earth.
note: Describes an Earth orbit with a period of one sidereal day, matching Earth’s rotation relative to the stars.

short: A mosque tower used for the call to prayer.
note: A tall, often slender tower associated with a mosque, traditionally providing a place from which the muezzin calls worshippers to prayer.

short: Unequalled; without a peer.
note: Borrowed from French, meaning without an equal or rival.

short: A queen who reigns in her own right.
note: A female sovereign exercising royal authority herself. “Regnant” means reigning, rather than merely being married to the reigning monarch.

short: The cone-shaped region of complete shadow.
note: The umbra is the part of a shadow from which the light source is entirely hidden. Behind a planet it forms a cone extending away from the Sun.

short: An apparent shift caused by a change of viewpoint.
note: The change in an object’s apparent position when observed from different locations. Astronomers use such angular shifts to measure distances.

short: A shrub or small tree with feathery foliage.
note: Plants of the genus Tamarix, with tiny scale-like leaves and clusters of small pale flowers. Many tolerate dry, salty environments.

short: A nearly massless, electrically neutral particle.
note: An elementary particle with a very small mass and no electric charge, which interacts only rarely with other matter.

short: A boundary beyond which no signal can escape.
note: The boundary of a black hole beyond which neither light nor other signals can escape to the outside universe.

short: A propagating ripple in spacetime.
note: A travelling disturbance of the gravitational field: a ripple in spacetime that carries energy away from its source.

short: A curved, single-edged Japanese sword.
note: A slightly curved sword with one cutting edge, traditionally associated with the samurai of Japan.

short: The visible, light-emitting layer of a star.
note: The luminous surface layer of the Sun or another star, from which most of its visible light emerges.

short: Loud electric warning horns.
note: Electrically operated horns or alarms. Klaxon was originally a trademark.

short: A substance that reduces damage from freezing.
note: An agent used to protect cells or other biological material against the harmful effects of freezing.

short: A traditional Māori fighting staff.
note: A close-combat weapon, usually of hardwood, with a carved head and projecting tongue at one end and a flattened striking blade at the other.

sources.label: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa: taiaha kura

short: A nearby red dwarf about six light-years away.
note: A small red dwarf in Ophiuchus, about six light-years from the Sun and closer than any stellar system except Alpha Centauri.

short: A closely packed formation of troops.
note: Originally a dense, ordered formation of ancient Greek infantry; more broadly, any massed body arranged in close ranks.

short: Below the range of human hearing.
note: Describes sound or vibration with a frequency lower than the human ear can normally hear.

short: Valves between the heart’s upper and lower chambers.
note: The mitral valve controls flow from the left atrium to the left ventricle; the tricuspid valve serves the corresponding right-side chambers and prevents backflow.

short: Small, light boats.
note: A general term for small boats, especially flat-bottomed rowing boats.

short: Wall-mounted holders for lights.
note: Brackets attached to a wall to support candles, torches, or similarly positioned lighting fixtures.

short: A large drinking or serving vessel.
note: A large container for wine or other drink, typically with a handle and spout and often a lid.

short: Traditional Japanese floor mats.
note: Mats traditionally made with straw and used as floor coverings in Japanese homes.

short: Another name for the sedative drug barbital.
note: The British name for barbital, a barbiturate historically used as a sedative and sleep-inducing drug.

short: The stellar layer between photosphere and corona.
note: A region of a star’s atmosphere lying above its visible photosphere and below the outer corona.

short: Matter made from the antiparticles of ordinary particles.
note: Antiparticles have the same masses as their corresponding particles but opposite electric charges where charged. Matter and antimatter can annihilate on contact, releasing energy.

short: Dense matter supported by quantum-mechanical pressure.
note: Matter compressed so strongly that quantum restrictions on how particles occupy states become important. Electron degeneracy pressure supports white-dwarf stars against gravitational collapse.

sources.label: NASA: white dwarfs and degenerate matter

short: Traditional Japanese swordsmanship.
note: Literally sword techniques: the Japanese arts of sword fighting from which modern kendo developed.

sources.label: All Japan Kendo Federation: history of kendo

short: Jurchen ruler who founded the Later Jin state.
note: Nurhaci (1559–1626) united Jurchen groups and proclaimed the Later Jin dynasty in 1616. His successors developed this state into the Qing dynasty.

sources.label: UC San Diego: transition from Ming to Qing

short: A district in northwestern Constantinople.
note: A quarter near the Golden Horn associated with an important church and a Byzantine palace complex that became a principal imperial residence.

sources.label: The Byzantine Legacy: palace of Blachernai

short: Dragon Well green tea from the Hangzhou region.
note: A Chinese green tea originating around Longjing village near Hangzhou, known for its flat leaves and fresh fragrance. West Lake Longjing is a particularly renowned variety.

short: Pluto’s largest moon.
note: Charon is about half Pluto’s diameter. The two bodies are mutually tidally locked, so each always presents the same face to the other.

short: Jupiter’s icy moon with evidence of a subsurface ocean.
note: One of the Galilean moons of Jupiter. Its icy surface overlies a likely saltwater ocean, making it an important target for investigating potentially habitable environments.

short: An astronomical unit, roughly 150 million kilometres.
note: A distance unit approximately equal to Earth’s average distance from the Sun, often used for dimensions and distances within a planetary system.

short: Einstein’s theory of gravity as spacetime geometry.
note: A theory in which mass and energy affect the geometry of spacetime, and that geometry determines the paths of freely moving bodies and light.

sources.label: Max Planck Institute: Einstein’s geometric gravity

short: Wedge-shaped written characters.
note: Characters made from arrangements of wedge-like strokes; cuneiform is a form of writing rather than the name of a spoken language.
